subject: Critical Thinking
title: Al-Khwarizmi: The Father of Algorithms
description: One-minute skill: Al-Khwarizmi: The Father of Algorithms.

hook.text: Every time your phone calculates a route, it runs an algorithm.

buildup.text: Working in Baghdad's House of Wisdom, Al-Khwarizmi wrote 'Al-Kitab al-Mukhtasar' – introducing algebra & systematic.

discovery.text: His method: reduce any problem to a standard form, then apply a step-by-step procedure to solve it.

twist.text: He preserved & advanced Greek & Indian mathematics when Europe had largely lost it.

climax.text: Algorithmic thinking: break complex problems into simple, repeatable steps.

punchline.text: Every algorithm running on every computer traces back to one idea: make.

quiz.question: What was Al-Khwarizmi's key contribution to thinking methods?

details.summary: Al-Khwarizmi, a 9th-century mathematician in Baghdad, developed algebra as a systematic discipline and created step-by-step problem-solving procedures that gave us the word 'algorithm.' His methods turned messy problems into repeatable procedures.
details.whyItMatters: Algorithmic thinking — breaking complex problems into repeatable steps — is the foundation of computer science, decision making, and any systematic approach to problem solving.
takeaways: Al-Khwarizmi's name gave us the word 'algorithm'
He systematized algebra as a formal discipline
Step-by-step procedural thinking originated from his methods

faq.question: What is the connection between Al-Khwarizmi and modern computing?
faq.answer: The word 'algorithm' derives from the Latin form of his name. His idea that any problem can be solved by following a precise sequence of steps is the conceptual foundation of every computer program ever written.

faq.question: How did Al-Khwarizmi change the way people solved mathematical problems?
faq.answer: Before Al-Khwarizmi, mathematical solutions were often ad hoc. He introduced systematic methods where the same steps could solve entire categories of problems, making mathematics a repeatable, teachable procedure rather than individual creativity.
